lf-diagram.description: A diagram rendered from a Mermaid-source body by Agentic Mermaid. It draws flowcharts, stateDiagram-v2, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram, and Mermaid's other families that Agentic Mermaid supports, such as gantt, timeline, and mindmap. The body is data, not prose: text inside its <pre>, HTML-escaped (& first, then the angle brackets). Flowcharts accept Mermaid's classic node shapes. Unstyled nodes already use Leaf's accent surface; give classDef only to a node that must stand apart from it, with one tone's whole fill/stroke/color set, such as `fill:var(--ok-tint),stroke:var(--ok),color:var(--ok-ink)`. The renderer also honors stroke-width and ignores other properties. Quote a label that holds its shape's closing bracket: `A["names: list[str]"]`, since the unquoted form is refused. The renderer parts from Mermaid where `version check --render` does not see it: it draws no `click` or `link` target and no frontmatter or sequence `title`, drops a state statement that ends in `;`, labels a state with its bare id when a transition names it before `state "…" as S0` declares it, reads an ER relationship only in its symbol form (`||--o{`), and draws an entity code such as `#36;` as written. The whole diagram is one Comment target. Boxes listed in `parts` as `node:SOURCE_ID` expose individual targets, where SOURCE_ID is the authored id of a flowchart node or subgraph, state or composite state, sequence participant, class, or ER entity. Unlisted boxes and diagrams authored without `parts` keep only the whole-diagram target. Edges, sequence messages, and chart marks have no stable source id and cannot be listed as parts.
lf-diagram.x-example:
flowchart LR
  Cart([Cart]) --> Pay{Paid?}
  Pay --> Receipt[(Receipt)]
  classDef done fill:var(--ok-tint),stroke:var(--ok),color:var(--ok-ink)
  class Receipt done
